Rooted in faith; enabling all to grow and flourish
Welcome to Clanfield CE Primary School
Welcome to Clanfield Church of England Primary Website. I hope you find the information contained here useful, whether you are a pupil having a peek at what other classes have been doing, a prospective parent deciding whether to send your child here, or an existing parent who cannot find the latest newsletter in your child’s bag! This website is updated frequently with latest news and information, calendar dates as well as a gallery of children’s displays, work and events. On the class pages you can see examples of super learning and explore termly curriculum information. Please visit regularly or perhaps set Clanfield Church of England Primary School as your home page!
Discover our schoolFrom Above
/i/video/Website_Video_-_October_2024_.mov
We are delighted to share with you the report from of our recent SIAMs (Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools) inspection. The report reflects the strong Christian vision that is at the heart of our school community and how this vision is deeply embedded and lived out daily by both staff and pupils.
A key highlight of the report is the recognition of our culture of compassion, wellbeing and inclusion which is central to our school’s ethos. The leadership team ensure that this is modelled at all levels, creating an environment where families feel understood, staff feel trusted, and pupils are able to thrive. The inspector also highlights how happy, confident, and caring our pupils are, with a strong belief that they can make a real difference in the world.
The report celebrates that staff are relentless in their pursuit to discover the best way to develop the good soil and through our inclusive curriculum offer, we ensure that every child has the opportunity to grow and flourish, regardless of their gifts or challenges.
There is much to celebrate in this report and we are incredibly proud of what we have achieved together in the last 6 years. We will continue to build upon this foundation to ensure that our school remains a place where both adults and children thrive in a supportive, caring, and inspiring environment.
Thank you for your ongoing support.

Music
Music at Clanfield CE Primary School
At Clanfield CE Primary School we believe that every child should have access to our Music Curriculum. Learning about music and having the opportunity to play instruments together is an important part of a rounded education. Music plays an important role in brain development and helps to develop language, motor skills, emotional intelligence and collaboration skills.
Our Curriculum follows the planning of 'SingUp' and we also provide the children with the opportunity to perform and access peripatetic music lessons in woodwind, brass, guitar and piano. We also work with 'iRock' to give the children the opportunity to perform together as a band.

PE & Sports Premium
Clanfield Church of England PE Vision
Clanfield Church of England Primary School works together with Get Set 4 PE to provide an inspirational environment for our children. Our PE lessons are planned using the Get Set 4 PE platform, which aligns with our values, whole child approach to Physical Education and the objectives laid out in the National Curriculum.
Our lessons ensure a structured and progressive approach to Physical Education. Pupils begin learning fundamental movement skills in EYFS and gradually progress to team sports and more complex activities in Key Stage 2. This approach helps all of our children to develop the physical literacy, emotional and thinking skills needed to achieve. We aim to inspire our children to enjoy and engage with Physical Education in line with our values of hope, courage and compassion.
Our curriculum creates an inclusive environment where our children feel included, valued, challenged and supported to reach their potential. The children have the opportunity to learn dance, gymnastics, football, swimming, netball, hockey, tennis, tag rugby and many more. Each year we celebrate our skills and development at our Sports Day event.
As our children move through our school we offer them the opportunity to represent the school in sporting events at Burford School through our relationship with the Burford Partnership programme. We also have visits from the Partnership to our school.

Sports Premium
The PE and Sport Premium is funding provided to primary schools to enhance the provision of PE and sport. It is for schools to decide how the PE and Sport funding is spent. Schools receive PE and sport premium funding based on the number of pupils in years 1 to 6.
At Clanfield CE Primary School we aim to use this funding to create a sustainable curriculum for all children throughout the school. Some of the funding has been invested in the professional development of staff to enhance the quality of teaching for all children.

School Dinners
Menu April 2026 to Oct 2026
Special Dietary Requirement Form
All school meals are prepared and cooked on-site by our kitchen team. Oxfordshire County Council (OCC) produce our meals and we work with them to develop a menu that fits with our Healthy Schools approach. If your child has any special dietary requirements please fill in the form above, and return to the school office.
All pupils in Reception and Years 1 and 2 are entitled to Universal Free School Meals. For pupils in Years 3 and above who are not in receipt of Free School Meals, the cost of a school meal is £2.90 per meal and this must be paid for online. Children can choose their school meals on a rolling 3-week basis and their order is placed directly with OCC. Please contact the school office if you have any questions about school meals.Should you feel that you are entitled to Free School Meals, please contact the school office. Please speak to the office even if your child is receiving Universal Free School Meals as Clanfield Church of England Primary School receives additional pupil funding for those entitled to Free School Meals. After you have completed your application you will receive an email to confirm your eligibility, you can then bring this into the school office as proof of your entitlement. Oxfordshire County Council will also send out a notification to us here at school confirming your child’s FSM and Pupil Premium eligibility.
Free School Meals Application
The Department for Education have a useful link https://www.gov.uk/apply-free-school-meals whereby parents can check whether their child can get free school meals and find out how to apply.
Pack Lunches – What you need to know
Eating well is important. Children need to eat well as it will give them energy and nutrients to grow and develop, be healthy and active. A healthy, enjoyable lunch gives children the energy they need to learn and play at school. Use the information on the Change for life website (below) to help make your child a healthier packed lunch.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clanfield Church of England Primary School - Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
Welcome to our page on special educational needs and disabilities. We hope the following information helps you understand how we value every child, no matter what their needs or starting points may be; how we identify and assess needs and put the right support in place; and how we remove barriers to them achieving their potential.
Our SENDCo is Mrs Jane Rawson (j.rawson@clanfield.oxon.sch.uk) and she is in school each Tuesday, during term time.
Our vision draws inspiration from the Parable of the Sower which is found in the gospel of Matthew 13:1-9, 18-23 in the New Testament. We aim to create ‘good soil’ for everyone to grow and flourish by promoting faith in themselves, faith in others, and the opportunity to consider faith in God. Our vision is to be a ‘Place to Flourish’ through Hope for the future, Compassion for all and Courage to face challenges to develop our individual talents and grow.
If the parable is considered in relation to the soil, there is another important theme for school life. For good things to grow, the soil must provide the right conditions for that growth. For children to flourish and produce good things, they need help to be ready to learn and encouragement to make the most of every opportunity.
This feeds into our attitude towards children who have additional needs. We are an inclusive mainstream Local Authority Church of England Primary School that fully complies with the requirements outlined in the Special Educational Needs Code of Practice (CoP, 2014) which can be found here:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/send
Our SEND Policy (please see school policy page) outlines our aims and all our arrangements for SEND co-ordination and management, including identification, assessment and provision.
Information for Parents and Carers - FAQs
What is SEND?
A child or young person has SEND if they have a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for him or her. A child of compulsory school age or a young person has a learning difficulty or disability if he or she:
What is the SEND Register?
When progress is made a child may be removed from the SEND register. Parents are always asked before their child is put onto the SEND register.
Who oversees SEND in this school?
The Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENDCo) is Mrs Jane Rawson. She works in collaboration with the Head teacher and class teachers, assisting in the development of inclusive classrooms and teaching practices and the day-to-day management of SEND in school. She will meet regularly to assess the progress of all children in the school and review whether a child needs additional support. There is a SEND link governor as well. In our school this is Mrs Olivia Hawkins.
Early Identification and Parental Input
The Code of Practice (2014, 5.5) says, ‘All those who work with young children should be alert to emerging difficulties and respond early. Parents know their children best and it is important that all practitioners listen and understand when parents express concerns about their child’s development. They should also listen to and address any concerns raised by children themselves.’ We believe that knowing the children we teach is vital and we believe that the child and their parents are the centre of the process.
How will I know if my child has SEND?
A child does not automatically have a Special Educational Need because they are making slow progress or are not doing as well as their peers. The focus is on children who need teaching that is ‘additional to or different from’ their peer group (CoP, 2014). Identifying SEND needs early is crucial and parents know their children best, so we have regular meetings with parents and rely on the information they provide us in helping us to identify if a child or young person has SEND.
The school uses Oxfordshire County Council’s SEND guidance and assessment tool as way of identifying if there is a Special Educational Need and what levels of support should be offered. The assessment tool helps us to make sure we are offering the provision expected from all schools in Oxfordshire. There are four broad areas of SEND:
Regular reviews are also carried out with teachers where the possibility of a child having SEND could be discussed. Further checks can be carried out, for example, detailed lesson observation by the SENDCo and a review of interventions the child has been part of so far.
We will also consider whether a further, more specialist, assessment for SEND is needed for example from another service provider, e.g. from an Educational Psychologist, Speech and Language Therapist or a Specialist Advisory Teacher.
Following further consultation with parents, and if a child meets the descriptors in the assessment tool, and after all the checks on teaching and learning have been carried out, then the child will be placed on the schools SEND register. This is shared with the Local Authority.
Communication and Interaction Needs (C&I)
Cognition and Learning Needs (C&L)
Social, Emotional and Mental Health Needs (SEMH)
Sensory and/or physical needs (S/P)
What provision is offered?
The Code of Practice specifies the use of a ‘graduated approach’ where a cycle of Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR) is described. This means support offered can be a little to a lot. Once a child is placed on the register an appropriate plans are put in place to support them. All children are unique, regardless of the category of SEND they have, so it is important that we respond to their individual need. Some children will respond well to seemingly minor adaptations to our inclusive teaching offer; others will need more specialist support and input. We work closely with outside agencies to help us to design the most appropriate package of support for children on our register.
Adaptations can include:
Children on the SEND register have a Pupil Profile which describes their strengths, the needs and individual barriers to learning. It also describes the provision that they will be receiving and will track progress through both formative and summative assessment. This will be reviewed three times a year as part of the APDR cycle.
SEN mini hub
In 2024 we developed our own mini hub. This is run by our SEN TA who has received training from 2 special schools. The headteacher over sees and monitors the work and the class teachers plan for the morning. Children have a flexible morning with a soft landing, movement break, visual timetable and indoor outdoor curriculum dependent on the needs of the pupil in the morning. The expectation is that the children are registered with their class ( their tribe) and the aim is that they will return to class when they are ready. The mini hub can support up to 4 children at a time. Children take part in phonics, english and maths activities and these are adapted on a day to day basis. The impact of this work so far is 4 children who accessed the mini hub last year are now in full time class in September 2025.
What is an EHCP?
An EHCP is short for an Education, Health and Care Plan. These are for children who have the most complex needs. They are created by the Local Authority in collaboration with parents and the school and the describe in detail the needs that the child has. This is reviewed annually in addition to the SEND reviews that take place three times a year. External agencies may also be invited to these annual reviews – for example if the child has speech and language therapy, the speech and language therapist will be invited.
It is vital that both the child’s voice and the parents’ views are central to this meeting and where appropriate the child can attend – especially for the first part of the meeting where the child's strength and achievements are celebrated.
How do you make provision for children with SEND at this school?
Some of the interventions we might use for Communication and Interaction are, turn taking social skills games, visual timetables, now and next boards, nurture groups, movement breaks/brain breaks and Social Stories to help with transitions and social situations.
At Clanfield we provide support for Cognition and Learning difficulties with small group and 1:1 phonics groups, Little Wandle Keep Up small groups, Precision Teaching, careful seating and pairing, coloured overlays / dyslexia friendly exercise books, outdoor learning, 1:1 reading, pre- teaching vocabulary, catch up Maths and Maths fluency groups, as well as a newer intervention - Number Stacks.
The provisions and interventions we use for Social, Emotional and Mental health are nurture, Drawing and Talking (https://drawingandtalking.com/), nurture, Zones of Regulation and also the blob tree, 1:1 support from TAs trained to listen, calm spaces, the Flower Room (a quiet area with calming activities, a sofa and space to reflect and talk). We have Senior Mental Health Leads (SMHL – Kim Rogers and Jane Rawson), have received extensive training and support from The Mulberry Bush (https://mulberrybush.org.uk/events-training/), and have bought in The Mulberry Bush’s SEMH curriculum – new for this year!
We use many other strategies, activities and tools to help with sensory or physical needs, such as alternatives to written formats e.g. ICT and Scribes, individual support for pupils with complex medical needs, appropriate training is given based on need, wobble cushions, lap weights, sloped writing tables, raised seating arrangement, quiet places to work or dens for quiet space, pencil grips and wrist weights, fine motor skills games.
How do we know our support is working?
We monitor our provision through reviews with parents, listening to your child’s voice, data analysis, work scrutiny and lesson observations. We may buy in consultants and outside agencies to help us do this. We monitor pupil progress through class reviews and review the success of interventions and provision maps.
How can I support my child?
Who can support me with my child’s SEND?
Having a child with SEND can be worrying and exhausting. The school recognises this and we want to help parents by working closely together. We also have access to other specialists. There are also lots of local and national support groups who have parent groups and networks and lots of useful tips. The SENDCo is always happy to talk to you to help you identify which direction to go in to access more help.
What are the school's arrangements for supporting pupils with SEND in transfer between phases of education?
We work closely with pupils and their families to make sure any change, such as moving classes or changing schools, is as smooth and positive as possible. We plan transitions carefully by sharing information with new teachers or schools, arranging extra visits, and preparing children in advance so they know what to expect. For older pupils, we help them develop important life skills such as independence, communication, and confidence. We also work with parents and outside professionals to support pupils as they prepare for adulthood, further education, or more independent living.
Who do I talk to if I am worried about my child or the provision offered?

Governor Members & Structure
Collecting and publishing Governing Board Diversity data
The governors of Clanfield CE School believe it is important that boards reflect the diversity of the school communities they serve. Diverse boards promote inclusive school environments and provide diverse role models for staff and young people.
The governors are currently collecting data on the diversity of the board, including data on age, gender and ethnicity. They will use that data to inform their recruitment and training needs and ensure there is always a diverse range of perspectives around the table to support robust decision making.
Due to our relatively small governing body we do not publish this diversity data online as individual governors could be identified and we have a legal obligation to protect their personal data.
Governor Declarations
An introduction from each member of our Governing Board
Mrs Kim Rogers - Headteacher
Committee: Headteacher
Term: First appointed on 01/09/2019 -
I have been in education for 30 years. I bring a wealth of senior leadership experience in primary schools including work as an Ofsted inspector, School Improvement Advisor for Oxford Diocesan Schools Trust and School Improvement Partner (SIP) for the local authority. I have significant experience as a governor and for 8 years I was a governor at my sons School. Most recently, I have been asked to support Stonesfield School in the role of Executive Headteacher and am enjoying the challenge of leading both schools.
I believe that every child deserves the very best provision and opportunities so that they can reach their full potential. I am passionate about ensuring the school continues to be a thriving part of the local community for many years to come. I live in West Oxford with my husband, 2 children. Portuguese water dog and enjoy running, cycling and yoga.
Mrs Zoe Thomas - Chair of Governors & Parent Governor
Committee: Chair of Governors, Chair of Curriculum Committee, Chair of Pay Committee, Resources Committee Member
Term: 06/09/2023 - 05/09/2027
First appointed: 06/09/2023
I became a Governor as I am passionate about ensuring that all children at Clanfield have the best opportunity to learn and develop. I have lived in Clanfield for over 10 years and have a daughter and twin boys at the school.
The majority of my career to date has been working in travel, where I had the opportunity to indulge my passion for travel as well as gaining a plethora of experience working in sales and leading teams. After taking a sabbatical, I decided on a career change and moved to the education sector working as a finance officer in a nearby primary school. This combined experience has definitely helped with my role as a governor.
Mrs Olivia Hawkins - Vice-Chair of Governors & Local Authority Governor
Committee: Vice-Chair of Governors, Curriculum Committee Member
Term: 01/09/2025 - 31/08/2029
First appointed: 01/09/2014
I work in the education sector directly with children and their families and also offer training and consultation in behaviour and communication to various organisations. My experience working in safeguarding and wellbeing led me to my role on the governing body because I am passionate about supporting the children and staff to thrive and enjoy their time at Clanfield.
Mr Andy Uglow - Co-Opted Governor
Committee: Resources Committee Member, Pay Committee Member
Term: 06/10/2022 - 05/10/2026
First appointed: 18/09/2018
As well as being a parent of two children who have attend Clanfield, I am an experienced secondary school leader with a specific interest in the development of excellence in the classroom, driven by evidence-based best practice. I am a member of Resources Committee and have specific responsibility for overseeing the very exciting work that is going into the development of the curriculum. In addition to my responsibilities in school, I serve as a founding Trustee of the Rafiki Thabo Foundation - a charity that provides educational support to young people in Lesotho, Kenya and Uganda.
Mrs Nicola Allen - Co-Opted Governor
Committee: Curriculum Committee Member
Term: 25/02/2026 - 24/02/2030
First appointed: 25/02/2026
I am parent of two children who attend the school and am passionate about supporting and empowering children to reach their full potential within a positive and inclusive environment.
I have worked within children’s services for the past 15 years and have extensive experience supporting children and young people with Special Educational Needs. Ofsted Inspection Reports
We are delighted to share our most recent Ofsted report with you.
Ofsted Inspection Report - February 2022
A Message from Mrs Rogers
I hope that by now you will have had time to read our glowing Ofsted report.
The process was extremely positive and useful in terms of looking at school improvement and the inspectors were very thorough in their inspection of our school. Ofsted have judged Clanfield CE Primary as a Good School and this is a fantastic achievement within the new framework especially given the journey we have been on. The inspectors talked very positively about the ethos of the school and our wonderful children. The inspectors described personal development as a strength of the school.
The whole staff team – and all stakeholders including Governors, OCC and the Diocese– have been committed to working tirelessly and determinedly towards providing our pupils with exciting and valuable opportunities that have been proven to lead to high quality achievement. We are very lucky that we work with children who are respectful, kind to each other, motivated to learn, curious about what there is still to know, and we are very proud that Her Majesty’s Inspectors have recognised this.
Congratulations, in the first instance, go to the children. The team met with children from all year groups and one of many highlights was hearing the inspectors report back on how positive they all are about their school. We also wish to thank parents. Your support for your children’s education is essential and was clearly reflected in the overwhelmingly positive online responses on Ofsted Parent View. The report also highlights the work of our Governing Body. Thank you governors past and present- your commitment and trust in us has been invaluable- without your passion, challenge and dedication to see all children achieve, school would not have been nearly as successful.
We are also incredibly proud of the hard work put in by every staff member every day. It is a real privilege to lead such an amazing team. I would like to use this opportunity to thank them for providing your children with a great education. Due to this hard work, inspectors noted that the school has been transformed and a couple of comments that really resonated with me were, ‘Clanfield is a harmonious place. Staff, pupils, parents, and carers all feel that they are part of one close-knit family. Happiness and joy are apparent everywhere. Pupils love learning’, The hard work has paid off, and Clanfield has transformed.
What is very satisfying is that all the areas listed were within the development plan prior to the inspection and there were no surprises during the day.
Our pupils’ potential to achieve amazing things in our community – and beyond – has been the motivation for staff. Every single person who works in school cares passionately about the life chances and potential of your children and what they may achieve after they leave us.
Teachers’ expectations of the standard of pupils’ handwriting fall below the national curriculum requirements. Some pupils struggle to write in a consistent style and present work neatly. Leaders need to establish a common approach to how pupils are taught handwriting.
Have a lovely weekendMrs Kim Rogers

pageCache.text:
Behaviour & Relationships
“Why crush behaviours with punishment when you can grow them with love? Visible consistency with visible kindness allows exceptional behaviour to flourish.”
Paul Dix, ‘When The Adults Change, Everything Changes’, 2017
At Clanfield Church of England Primary School, we aim to grow positive behaviours with love in a happy, safe, caring, stimulating and inclusive environment for all.
Promoting good behaviour amongst the pupils is a shared responsibility. All those who work with the school, governors, parents, the wider community and the children, all have a vital role to play.
As members of the school community, all stakeholders should build positive relationships with each other and we expect each individual to respect others, their families, culture and beliefs, as part of the exceptionally high standards of behaviour that we have at Clanfield Church of England Primary School.
We have a Behaviour and Relationship policy which puts relationships at the heart of everything we do. We believe that implementing the principles of Restorative Practice helps us to focus on building better relationships with each other, taking the time to ensure that every member of our school community feels listened to, valued and respected. All our staff have been trained in Restorative conversations and we support pupils in developing the skills to maintain positive relationships with others and to resolve disagreements and problems themselves. It is our role to educate our pupils to understand how their behaviour affects others and its impact on others. Pupils are supported to identify ways they can put right the harm they have caused. We are helping them to become empathic, considerate people who have the skills to avoid and resolve problems independently.

Early Reading & Phonics
Reading lies at the heart of the curriculum at Clanfield CE School. We are dedicated to enabling our pupils to become lifelong readers and it is our intention every child at Clanfield CE School has the opportunity to love books and love reading.
READING
Phonics
How we teach phonics
Parent Phonics Support Video
The video below explains what phonics is and how it is taught in school, guiding parents through the key approaches we use to help children learn to read and write. We hope you find it useful.
Phonics and Handwriting Workshop
Reading practice sessions
How do we assess phonic knowledge?
By KS2, we expect all pupils to be ready for the whole class reading sessions which are undertaken at least 4 times a week. We use a VIPERS strategy to reinforce teaching of vocabulary, inference, prediction, evaluation, recall and summary. The focus here is on vocabulary development, the development of specific reading skills and immersion in a wide range of texts. These lessons use class novels as a stimulus for deeper thinking and link a range of fiction and non-fiction texts to these in order to further develop contextual knowledge and understanding. Children use reading journals to record their ideas and answers to comprehension questions.
Lesson structure in Year 3 / 4
Lesson structure in Year 5 /6
Over a year, children will have access to a range of different texts which have been carefully chosen in order for children to successfully navigate reading with confidence. These are based on Doug Lemouv 5 plagues of the developing reader. We believe, if we expose pupils to books that feature these complexities we are ensuring rigour in their reading which then prepares them for the next stage of their education.

We also promote reading for pleasure as this itself plays a major role within reading development. Each day the children will be read aloud to. This is often held before or after lunch so that it does not get missed off the busy day. In Reception, a story is usually enjoyed during snack time. Each class has a well-stocked library and books are celebrated regularly with recommendations from teachers. Our reading environment also promotes the whole school love of reading.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clanfield Church of England Primary School - Maths
pageCache.text:
Maths
"It's not a boring place to be, the mathematical world. It's an extraordinary place; it's worth spending time there." Marcus du Sautoy
At Clanfield CE Primary School, we aspire to nurture individuals with the power to make a difference. We aim to create 'good soil' for everyone to grow and flourish by promoting faith in themselves, faith in others, and the opportunity to consider faith in God. Our vision is to be a 'Place to Flourish' through Hope for the future, Compassion for all and Courage to face challenges to develop our individual talents and grow.
At Clanfield, we believe that every child has the potential to succeed in mathematics. Our aim is to provide all learners with the opportunity to flourish through a rich, engaging and well-sequenced mathematics curriculum that nurtures curiosity and confidence. We strive to develop lively and enquiring minds that can reason mathematically, communicate ideas effectively and apply understanding to a range of contexts. Mathematics at Clanfield is seen as a fascinating subject that explores number, space, pattern and relationships, requiring not only factual knowledge and procedural fluency but also deep conceptual understanding gained through exploration, application and discussion. Through our approach, we aim to develop resilient, confident and capable learners who make rich connections between mathematical ideas and develop a life-long love of learning in mathematics. Through a mastery approach, we aim to ensure children develop a deeper understanding of key mathematical concepts in small progressive steps. Our teaching sequences address the three main aims of the National Curriculum: fluency, reasoning and problem solving. We aim to ensure all pupils:
At Clanfield, our curriculum is based on the Curriculum Prioritisation Materials from the National Centre of Excellence in the Teaching of Mathematics (NCETM), supported by the Oak Academy teaching materials. Learning is split into units that are taught in a sequence whereby previous learning can be used to support new learning. The sequence in which the units are taught also supports the teaching of, and the children's ability to create, links between different concepts and therefore deepen their understanding.
In EYFS and Key Stage 1, we use the Mastering Number programme, which builds number sense and fluency, giving the children strong foundations on which they can build on in later years. Early years staff enhance this core programme with additional challenges and wider elements of the EYFS framework, ensuring a rich, balanced mathematical experience. Activities are carefully planned to promote mathematical talk, reasoning and problem solving through purposeful play and adult-led learning.
In Key Stage 1, maths is taught in single year groups, following best practice guidance from the NCETM. In Key Stage 2, we follow the NCETM two year rolling programme for the teaching of mathematics to ensure high quality teaching and learning for our mixed age classes.
Maths is taught daily using a consistent lesson structure from Year 1 to Year 6. Our maths lessons are carefully structured to build on prior learning and ensure progression in understanding. Each lesson begins by making explicit links to previous learning, helping pupils to connect new concepts to what they already know. Key mathematical vocabulary is then revisited or introduced to support understanding and accurate communication. New learning is delivered through a gradual release model - I do, we do, you do - where the teacher first models the concept, then guides pupils through shared practice, before allowing them to apply their understanding independently. Lessons provide rich opportunities for pupils to deepen their learning through reasoning, problem solving and exploring variation, enabling all learners to develop fluency, flexibility and confidence in their mathematical thinking.
In addition to the daily mathematics lesson, each class in Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 takes part in a short fluency session four times per week. These sessions are designed to consolidate and reinforce previously taught concepts, providing pupils with regular opportunities to practise and strengthen their understanding. The focus is on developing fluency and accuracy through repeated practice, enabling children to recall and apply key mathematical facts with confidence and automaticity.
